messages:
Marta: Heads-up: after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak (auto-kernel-v2) we saw a ~7% drop in KV prefix cache hit-rate on prod6 during the 09:00-11:00 window. Correlation looks strong with a spike in small unique prefixes and higher frag counts.

Jonah: ugh, saw alerts. Any idea whether it's the kernel switch itself or an accidental key normalization change?

Marta: Initial traces suggest key production changed. The hash ordering in the new kernel path moves non-deterministic whitespace handling earlier, so similar prompts got different canonical keys. Example from logs: 

```
old_key: user:instr:translate|en->fr|prefix_hash:abc123
new_key: user:instr:translate |en->fr|prefix_hash:abc123
```

Small trailing spaces ended up in the new_key, blowing up hotset.

Alex: That explains hit-rate. Fix could be either canonicalization normalization or stronger warmup + TTL policies to absorb the churn. Which is faster?

Marta: Short-term patch: normalize prompt before hashing (trim + collapse whitespace). Medium-term: explore adaptive TTL-shedding to avoid immediate OOM/frag when hotset shifts.

Sarah: Can you outline TTL-shedding? Sounds novel.

Marta: Idea: when memory pressure > X% and eviction rate rising, automatically shorten TTL for low-EWMA-hit prefixes so they clear faster. Keeps true hot prefixes intact. High level: 
- Maintain per-prefix EWMA hit rate (alpha=0.2)
- If cluster memory_pressure > 85%: for prefixes with EWMA < 0.1, set TTL = max(min_ttl, current_ttl * 0.25)
- Allow TTL ramp back to default when pressure subsides and EWMA improves

Jonah: How do we avoid oscillation (rapid TTL flips)?

Marta: Add hysteresis: cooldown window 10m after a TTL change; require sustained pressure for rampdown; require sustained EWMA improvement for rampup. Also apply jitter so we don't change many prefixes in one tick.

Alex: We should also check kernel-side metadata size. The new kernel path adds 8 bytes of per-entry header (align/counter). Under high fragment counts that can cause slab splits and worsen fragmentation. If header bloat + higher unique prefixes => OOM faster.

profiler-bot: profile snapshot uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood/profiler/3076543210/kv-frag-snapshot.html (summary: per-entry meta +8B on new kernel; median key len +3 bytes due to trailing whitespace).

Sarah: Good catch. So two fixes: canonicalization to reduce unique keys, and TTL-shedding to mitigate until warmup happens. Propose we do both but ship canonicalization first.

Marta: Agreed. Plan: 
1) Patch runtime to normalize prompt keys in kernel-selection branch (PR#5123). Quick rollback path ready. Target: today EOD for canary.
2) Implement TTL-shedding as runtime config toggle (opt-in) and run as experiment on prod6 for 6h if canary stabilizes.
3) Add a short-term kernel build that removes the extra 8B header (optimize metadata packing) for evaluation; if it reduces frag by >4% we push.

Jonah: For the TTL config, what knobs? Need safe defaults.

Marta: Suggest config example: 

```json
{
  "ttl_shedding": {
    "enabled": true,
    "memory_pressure_threshold": 0.85,
    "ewma_alpha": 0.2,
    "low_hit_threshold": 0.1,
    "min_ttl_seconds": 30,
    "shedding_factor": 0.25,
    "cooldown_seconds": 600,
    "jitter_pct": 0.15
  }
}
```

Alex: Nice. Add a safety clamp: never drop TTL below 30s for prefixes seen >50QPS average to avoid user-visible churn.

Marta: Good call. I'll add the clamp. Also will emit metrics: ttl_changes, prefixes_shed, average_ewma_before, post_shed_hitrate, evictions_rate.

Sarah: For the experiment, let's set up A/B rollout: 10% traffic on prod6 with TTL-shedding ON, 90% OFF. Monitor evictions and latency tail. If evictions decrease and tail latencies don't increase, scale to 50% then 100%.

profiler-bot: baseline metrics (09:00-11:00): hit_rate=0.72, frag_ratio=0.18, evictions_per_min=420.

Jonah: Who owns kernel canonicalization PR?

Marta: I'll own PR#5123. Jonah can own TTL-shedding feature flag and rollout. Alex will vet the metadata-packing patch. Sarah will monitor dashboards and approve scale-ups.

Alex: One more thought: batcher heuristics. With more unique small prefixes, continuous batching falls apart because tokens don't share KV cache and sequence lengths vary. We should enable a temporary batching relaxation for smaller batches to reduce kernel overhead while hotset stabilizes. Small change in batcher config might reduce CPU overhead.

Marta: Add to action items.

Action items: 
- Marta: open PR#5123 (canonicalize keys) and canary it today.
- Jonah: implement TTL-shedding toggle + metrics, start 10% experiment if canary OK.
- Alex: prototype metadata-packing change and run frag sim.
- Sarah: monitor prod6 dashboard and watch tail latency + evictions.

Marta: I'll post updates in this thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Jonah: Thanks — will start TTL code today.

Sarah: Ping me when canary is live, I'll watch the alerting channels.

profiler-bot: scheduled re-profile in 2h.
